messages.subject: WC-00188 Cryovance - the clause 11.3 problem (and now a SECOND excursion)
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah,

Two things.

(1) There has now been a SECOND excursion - batch DS-2025-047, collected 9 October. Driver left the validated route and switched off the refrigeration during a rest break; peak 14.1C. Also destroyed. So we now have two batches gone: 1,420,000 + 1,165,000 = 2,585,000 of product, plus re-manufacture/expediting (~612k) and QP/disposal (~89k). Direct losses ~3,286,000.

(2) Clause 11.3 caps Cryovance's liability at the greater of 500,000 or charges paid in the prior 12 months (which were 430,000). So unless we get round 11.3 we're capped at 500k against a 3.3m loss.

My view: two routes - construction (11.3 doesn't reach the core clause 4 cold-chain obligations) and UCTA reasonableness. The second excursion AFTER we warned them is gold for the reasonableness argument. Worth getting counsel early.

Tom

messages.plaintextBody:
Agreed on both. The repeat after notice is the whole case - it turns this from a one-off mechanical failure into a pattern. Let's instruct Harriet Stanford at Eldon for an advice on merits and on defeating 11.3. Get her the agreement, both data loggers, the QP assessments and the correspondence.

Send the letter before action once the second QP assessment is finalised. Make the LBA open and demand the vehicle/driver/CAPA records.

Sarah
